newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Camdessus says time to resume Russian lending.
newsitem.headline: Camdessus says time to resume Russian lending.

text.p: It is time for the International Monetary Fund to resume lending to Russia to back Moscow's economic reforms, IMF Managing Director Michel Camdessus said on Wednesday.
Camdessus also said in a lecture to students at an international affairs institute that he expected Russian inflation to slow to single digits in 1998.
Camdessus said the IMF had granted Russia a $10 billion three-year Extended Fund Facility loan last year, when uncertainties were greater than they are today.
"Why would we shy away now from continuing extending our support to Russia?" he asked.

"This is also the time for us, in the international community, to go ahead with our support for the completion of your reforms...by resuming our financing and risking our resources once again in support of your programme: a signal the markets expect, a signal your programme deserves," he said.
The IMF has repeatedly suspended monthly payments of the loan because it is worried by the low level of Russian tax revenues, which Camdessus said was serious.
